pages.quiz:
ENGLISH ACTIVITIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #3
====

GRADE: Grade 3
SUBJECT: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. No full stops
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

2. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goed
   B. went
   C. goes
   D. going

3. When practising Punctuation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Punctuation.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Punctuation.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Punctuation.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Punctuation.

4. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. Only a describing word
   C. Only an action
   D. A person, place, thing, or idea

5. When practising Connected text and fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Connected text and fluency.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Connected text and fluency.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Connected text and fluency.

6. When practising Language Activities at home, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Language Activities at home.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Activities at home.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Language Activities at home.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Language Activities at home.

7. When practising Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Comprehension.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Comprehension.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Comprehension.

8. When practising Guided Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Guided Writing.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Guided Writing.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Guided Writing.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Guided Writing.

9. When practising Spelling, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Spelling.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Spelling.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Spelling.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Spelling.

10. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. happiness
   C. quickly
   D. blue

11. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library
   B. where is the library
   C. Where is the Library
   D. Where is the library?

12. When practising Word Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Word Reading.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Word Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Word Reading.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Handwriting and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Spelling and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Punctuation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — One main idea with supporting sentences

2. B — went

3. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Punctuation.

4. D — A person, place, thing, or idea

5. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.

6. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Activities at home.

7. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.

8. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Guided Writing.

9. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Spelling.

10. A — run

11. D — Where is the library?

12. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Handwriting; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Spelling; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Punctuation; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Guided Writing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
